prompt: How much of the revenue from registered customers in January to June 2025 came from each tenth of those customers? Take the orders with order_ts from 1 January to 30 June 2025 (order_ts holds UTC time; both days included, in UTC) that have a customer_id; guest orders have a missing customer_id and do not count. A customer's revenue is the sum over the lines of the customer's orders of quantity times unit_price_eur minus line_discount_eur. Sort the customers from the highest revenue down and split them into ten groups whose sizes differ by at most one, the larger groups first: decile 1 holds the top spenders. When customers tie on revenue, the lower customer_id comes first. Return three columns, in this order: decile, customers (the number of customers in the decile) and revenue_share_pct, the decile's revenue as a percentage of all these customers' revenue, rounded to 1 decimal. Return one row for each decile. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, total each registered customer's revenue, split the customers into ten groups from the highest revenue, then add up each group's revenue as a share of the whole.
The groups hold the same number of customers, not the same revenue; the share needs the total over all deciles, which a window over the grouped rows can give.
why_this_works: NTILE(10) puts the same number of customers in each decile, and the window total over the grouped rows shows how unequal their revenue shares are.
